ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, point C is a point on the semicircle above AB, point D is the midpoint of the semicircle below AB. The segments AC, BC, and AD are connected, and through point D, DE is drawn parallel to AB and intersects the extension of CB at point E. If AD equals $5 \sqrt{2}$, what is the maximum value of the product of AC and CE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect CD and BD, \\
$\because$ DE$\parallel$AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABC=$\angle$E, \\
$\because$ $\angle$ABC=$\angle$CDA, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$E =$\angle$CDA, \\
$\because$ point D is the midpoint of the semicircle below AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACD=$\angle$DCE, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD\sim \triangle DCE$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CD}{CE}=\frac{AC}{CD}$, \\
$\therefore$ $CD^{2}=AC\cdot CE$, \\
$\because$ point D is the midpoint of the semicircle below AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ADB=$90^\circ$, BD=AD=$5\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ $AB=\sqrt{AD^{2}+BD^{2}}=10$, \\
$\because$ $CD\le AB=10$, \\
$\therefore$ $AC\cdot CE\le 10^{2}=\boxed{100}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, point C is a point on the semicircle above AB, point D is the midpoint of the semicircle below AB. The segments AC, BC, and AD are connected, and through point D, DE is drawn parallel to AB and intersects the extension of CB at point E. If AD equals $5 \sqrt{2}$, what is the maximum value of the product of AC and CE?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect CD and BD, \\
$\because$ DE$\parallel$AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABC=$\angle$E, \\
$\because$ $\angle$ABC=$\angle$CDA, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$E =$\angle$CDA, \\
$\because$ point D is the midpoint of the semicircle below AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACD=$\angle$DCE, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD\sim \triangle DCE$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CD}{CE}=\frac{AC}{CD}$, \\
$\therefore$ $CD^{2}=AC\cdot CE$, \\
$\because$ point D is the midpoint of the semicircle below AB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ADB=$90^\circ$, BD=AD=$5\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ $AB=\sqrt{AD^{2}+BD^{2}}=10$, \\
$\because$ $CD\le AB=10$, \\
$\therefore$ $AC\cdot CE\le 10^{2}=\boxed{100}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, and the center O is on AB; C is on the semicircular arc above AB; D is on the semicircular arc below AB, located approximately at the lower midpoint; line segments AC, BC, and AD have been drawn; CB is extended to the lower right to E; through D draw a horizontal line DE, parallel to AB, and intersecting the extension of CB at E.

Reasoning: Add auxiliary lines CD and BD according to the method. Because DE ∥ AB, and C, B, E are collinear, ∠E equals ∠ABC. Also because ∠ABC and ∠CDA are both inscribed angles subtending the same arc AC, ∠ABC = ∠CDA, therefore ∠E = ∠CDA. Since D is the midpoint of the lower semicircular arc, arc AD = arc DB, so ∠ACD and ∠DCE are equal. Thus △ACD ∼ △DCE. From similar triangles, CD/CE = AC/CD can be obtained, therefore AC·CE = CD^2.

Next, D is the midpoint of the lower semicircular arc, so AD = BD. Also AB is a diameter, so ∠ADB = 90°. It is known that AD = 5√2, therefore BD = 5√2, hence AB = √(AD^2 + BD^2) = √(50 + 50) = 10. Because CD is a chord in the same circle, its length does not exceed the diameter AB, so CD ≤ 10. Therefore AC·CE = CD^2 ≤ 10^2 = 100. Equality can be attained when CD is a diameter, so the maximum value is 100.
